data.summary: Fleet briefs tell a subagent to run 'ddflow --agent X brief --for-agent X <ITEM>' and follow it exactly; 'ddflow brief' takes only --item, --phase and --check-recovery, so the command exits 2 with an argparse usage error, and the positional item id fails the same way. The subagent has to fall back to 'brief --item' plus the driver doc. Either add the flag (brief for an agent: its item, its leftovers, its gates) or stop the briefs naming it.

chunk_findings.detail: `changed_phrases` spawns git subprocesses per changed `.py` file: up to two `_diff` calls (`base...tip` and, when `tip == "HEAD"`, `HEAD`) plus one `W.git(..., "ls-files", ...)` per iteration. The intent says the recall replay was widened to 40 merges; a merge touching N `.py` files therefore costs ~3·N git processes. For a merge touching 200 Python files that is ~600 process spawns per merge and ~24 000 across 40 merges, each git call reading the index/repo, so `changed_phrases` alone can turn selection from sub-second into minutes. Nothing bounds `files` and no single `git diff base...tip -- <files>` is reused, so a large refactor merge (e.g. a rename/reformat sweep touching most of `ddflow/`) is the input that makes the new route pathologically slow.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testidents.py `changed_phrases`

chunk_findings.detail: The diff-line filter drops any content line whose text begins with `--` or `++`, mistaking it for the `--- a/...` / `+++ b/...` file headers. A source line such as a SQL comment inside a triple-quoted literal (`-- fetch rows`), an ASCII-art banner inside a string, or a removed line that is literally `--` becomes `--- fetch rows` after the leading `-` is added, matches `ln[:3] == "---"`, and is silently discarded. The phrase extracted from that literal never enters `phrases`, so a test that asserts on the reworded/removed message is no longer selected — exactly the recall miss this change is meant to close, reproduced whenever a changed/lost string literal contains a line starting with `--` or `++`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testidents.py `changed_phrases` (the `ln[:3] not in ("---", "+++")` filter)

chunk_findings.detail: `_bare` is consulted for *every* import name that `resolve` cannot match, with no check that the name is actually meant to be a local module. It returns any same-stem `.py` found in a non-package ancestor directory, so external (stdlib/third-party) imports get false edges whenever a helper file happens to share the name. Concrete input: a repo whose `tests/` has no `__init__.py` and contains a fake `tests/queue.py`, plus `tests/test_worker.py` that does `import queue` for the stdlib module. `resolve("queue", g.names)` returns `""` (the file's module name is `tests.queue`), so `_bare("queue", "tests/test_worker.py", homes)` returns `tests.queue`, and the graph gains the edge `tests/test_worker.py -> tests.queue`. Changing the fake helper now selects `test_worker.py`, which never imports it — exactly the "noisy" over-selection this selector is supposed to avoid (`import mock`, `import select`, `import typing`, `import types`, … collide the same way). Over-selection of unrelated tests also inflates every gate run that touches such a helper. There is no allowlist/verification that the bare name is not a resolvable external module (e.g. via `importlib.util.find_spec`), so the new route can only add false positive edges.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testreach.py:96 (`_bare`) / :86 (`_bare_homes`)

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds a selection route based on matching words of string literals gained/lost in a source diff (`TI.changed_phrases` → `TI.phrase_tests`). Per [D-gap-affected-tests-no-partial] the affected-tests gap is explicitly scoped to the import-graph closure ("B-gap-affected-tests builds the import-graph closure only"); lexical string-literal matching is not part of that closure, so this widens the affected-tests criterion beyond the recorded decision. Demonstration: changing one line from `encoding="utf-8"` to `encoding="UTF-8"` in a source file yields a phrase (`utf-8`) that appears in most test files; the selector then pulls those tests in through a non-import-graph route, which is a criterion the decision says this gap must not use.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testselect.py:252 (`pick.many(TI.phrase_tests(...))`, new phrase route) [D-gap-affected-tests-no-partial]

chunk_findings.detail:
The change deletes `MERGES = 4` and collapses the two separate quantities into a single `SCAN = 40`, which the new comment calls "merges replayed (those with both source and tests in them)" while the docstring still says the test "Replays the last SCAN merges of THIS repository". These were previously *different* numbers, and the removed comment records why: with a scan window of `SCAN = 40`, exactly `MERGES = 4` merges had both source and tests and were actually replayed. So the single constant cannot mean both things at once, and either reading is wrong:
- If the loop still iterates the last `SCAN` merges and keeps the ones that have both source and tests (which is what the docstring "the last SCAN merges … (those with both source and tests in them)" says), then the replay count is again only a handful (~4), not 40 — exactly the "four were too few" failure the changelog claims to fix — while `ABSOLUTE_FLOOR` is raised from 0.7 to 0.85 on that same tiny sample.
- If the loop instead scans until 40 qualifying merges are found, then the docstring's "Bounded (`SCAN` merges, a few processes, no network)" guarantee is false: the scan is bounded by the repository's history length, not by `SCAN`, so on a repo with few qualifying merges the replay can walk the whole log.

Demonstrating input: the merge history the old comment describes (40 consecutive merges of which only 4 touch both source and tests) — under the first reading the new test replays 4 merges with a stricter floor, under the second it is not bounded by `SCAN` merges at all.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_recall.py:40

chunk_findings.detail: `_FILE_HEAD` only matches the unquoted form `diff --git a/... b/...`. With git's default `core.quotePath=true`, any path containing a non-ASCII byte (or `"`, `\`, a control char) is printed quoted, including the `a/`/`b/` prefixes: `diff --git "a/tests/t\303\253st.py" "b/tests/t\303\253st.py"`. The regex then does not match, so `current` is never reassigned and `started` is still `True` from the previous file in the same batch; the quoted file's `--- "a/..."` / `+++ "b/..."` header lines (they start with `-`/`+`) and every added/removed content line are appended to the *previous* file's list (`elif started and line[:1] in "+-"`). Concretely: a merge that reworded a CLI string in `tests/tëst.py` (or in a source module whose filename has a non-ASCII byte) yields `phrase -> <wrong file>`, so the new phrase route selects the wrong tests / still misses the regression test — exactly the miss this change is meant to close. The old per-file code never parsed the header (`_diff(tree, spec, "--", f)` plus `ln[:3] not in ("---","+++")`), so it was immune. (Secondary: because the two copies of the path are identical, a path containing the literal ` b/`, e.g. `x b/y.py`, makes the greedy `.*` split at the last ` b/`, i.e. inside the second copy, and group(1) becomes `y.py`.)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testidents.py:_FILE_HEAD / _added_removed

chunk_findings.detail: Untracked status is now decided by comparing `files` against the string output of `git ls-files -- <batch>` instead of the old quoting-agnostic `git ls-files --error-unmatch -- <f>` exit code. `ls-files` applies the same C-quoting as `diff`, so for `tests/tëst.py` it prints `"tests/t\303\253st.py"`, which never equals the key; the path therefore stays in `untracked`, the code reads the tracked file's whole working-tree content, and every one of its lines is fed to `_phrases` as if the merge had added them. The result is a set of phrases that have nothing to do with the change, expanding the selected test set (noise) for any repo with such a filename.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testidents.py:changed_phrases (untracked detection)

chunk_findings.detail: `_FILE_HEAD = re.compile(r"^diff --git a/.* b/(.*)$")` hard-codes git's default `a/`/`b/` prefixes and does not handle quoted paths, but `_added_removed` never gets a guarantee about the format of `git diff` output. Concrete failure: with `git config diff.mnemonicPrefix true` (or `diff.noprefix true`), `git diff <base>...HEAD -- src/x.py` emits `diff --git c/src/x.py w/src/x.py` (or `diff --git src/x.py src/x.py`), `_FILE_HEAD.match` fails for every file, `current` stays `None`, every `@@`/`+`/`-` line hits `elif current is None: continue`, so `_added_removed` returns `{}` and `changed_phrases` returns `{}`. The phrase route then contributes nothing and the very miss it was added for (`test_asagent_tree.py` reached only via a hub) is missed again, silently. The same regex also fails on git-quoted paths (non-ASCII, `"` or `\` in the name, `core.quotePath=true` default): `diff --git "a/caf\303\251.py" "b/caf\303\251.py"` does not match, so if that file is first its changed literals are dropped entirely, and if it is not first its `+`/`-` lines are appended to the *previous* file's list, because `current`/`started` are only reset inside the non-matching branch — producing phrases attributed to the wrong changed file. Fixing this needs either normalizing the header (e.g. `--no-prefix`/`-p` with an explicit `-c diff.mnemonicPrefix=false`, plus parsing quoted `b/...` names) or a prefix-agnostic header regex.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testidents.py :: `_FILE_HEAD` / `_added_removed`

chunk_findings.detail: The new fallback is only consulted when `resolve` returns falsy, so a bare name that matches *any* top-level module of the repo is bound to that module even when pytest would bind it to a sibling file of the importing test. `_bare_homes`'s docstring explicitly promises the case `import conftest` == `tests/conftest.py`, but with the very common layout of a root `conftest.py` **and** `tests/conftest.py`, `known` holds `conftest -> conftest.py`, `resolve("conftest", g.names)` succeeds, `_bare` never runs, and the recorded edge is `conftest` (root file) → the importing test. Concrete input: root `conftest.py`, `tests/conftest.py` defining `def make_client()`, and `tests/test_x.py` containing `from conftest import make_client` (pytest's prepend import mode puts `tests/` at `sys.path[0]`, so at run time the test really loads `tests/conftest.py`). Change only `tests/conftest.py`: the graph has no path from `tests.conftest` to `tests/test_x.py`, so `test_x` is not selected and the regression test is missed — the exact failure mode this change exists to fix. The same holds for any top-level collision, e.g. a repo package `helpers/` at the root plus a `tests/helpers.py` shadowing it.

chunk_findings.detail: The guard's stated rationale ("``import queue`` is the library's, whatever tests/ holds") does not hold in the environment this graph models: pytest's default prepend import mode inserts the test file's basedir at `sys.path[0]`, so a module in that directory shadows the stdlib one. Input: `tests/queue.py` with `VALUE = 1` and `tests/test_q.py` containing `import queue; assert queue.VALUE == 1` — under `pytest` this passes, proving `import queue` in that file binds to `tests/queue.py`. chunk_findings.detail: The old loop stopped after `MERGES` replayable merges (`if replayed >= MERGES: break`), which is what made this a "recall replay over the 40 newest merges". Concretely, on a repo with 500 merges this launches 500 `ProcessPoolExecutor` tasks, each running `_replay`/`_replayed` (git extraction of the source diff plus a full `T.select` pass), instead of 40; the pool is created and joined inside the test, so the suite's wall time grows with total repo history and is bounded only by `WORKERS`, which is a clear CI-timeout/regression risk. It also silently changes the measured quantity: `total`/`held` and the `ABSOLUTE_FLOOR` assertion are now computed over all history rather than the newest 40, so old merges the selector handles poorly can drag `held / total` below the floor and turn an intended recent-history regression guard into a flaky, historical one. The phrase route then contributes nothing and the very miss it was added for (`test_asagent_tree.py` reached only via a hub) is missed again, silently. The same regex also fails on git-quoted paths (non-ASCII, `"` or `\` in the name, `core.quotePath=true` default): `diff --git "a/caf\303\251.py" "b/caf\303\251.py"` does not match, so if that file is first its changed literals are dropped entirely, and if it is not first its `+`/`-` lines are appended to the *previous* file's list, because `current`/`started` are only reset inside the non-matching branch — producing phrases attributed to the wrong changed file. chunk_findings.detail: `_bare` only ever resolves the *first dot-segment* of an import name (`head = name.split(".", maxsplit=1)[0]`) — it is, as its own docstring says, for a *bare* name. Swapping the operands so that `_bare(...)` is tried before `resolve(...)` therefore changes behavior not just for bare imports but for every dotted one too, and it makes the truncated answer win over the precise one. Concrete case: `tests/test_x.py` contains `import ddflow.services.testidents` (equally `from ddflow.services.testidents import X`). The loop passes `n = "ddflow.services.testidents"`, `_bare` computes `head = "ddflow"`, scans `PurePosixPath("tests/test_x.py").parents` = `tests`, `.`, and returns `homes[(".", "ddflow")]` — i.e. the `ddflow` package module — instead of the submodule. Because `_bare` is now first, `resolve("ddflow.services.testidents", g.names)` is never called, so the graph gets an edge `test_x -> ddflow/__init__.py` and loses the edge `test_x -> ddflow/services/testidents.py` that the old `resolve(...) or _bare(...)` order produced. A later change to `ddflow/services/testidents.py` then does not select `test_x` (unless the package `__init__` happens to import the submodule), which is precisely the under-selection class this delta is supposed to fix. The sibling-shadowing fix only needs to apply to single-segment names (e.g. `import queue` → `tests/queue.py`), so the call should remain `resolve`-first when `"." in n`.

data.body:
Fixes bug Bbec4f122e7: Fleet briefs tell a subagent to run 'ddflow --agent X brief --for-agent X <ITEM>' and follow it exactly; 'ddflow brief' takes only --item, --phase and --check-recovery, so the command exits 2 with an argparse usage error, and the positional item id fails the same way. The subagent has to fall back to 'brief --item' plus the driver doc. Either add the flag (brief for an agent: its item, its leftovers, its gates) or stop the briefs naming it. Found on fix-Bb5b8b17161.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Bbec4f122e7 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Bbec4f122e7 --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug Bbec4f122e7: brief has no --for-agent flag; the fleet instruction names one

data.body:
